bull.b: Sustained positive operating cash flow and improving free cash flow provide durable internal funding for capital projects, dividends, and buybacks. This cash-generation ability reduces reliance on external financing and supports long-term investment in resorts and shareholder returns.

High-margin performance across Las Vegas, Macau and Boston reflects a diversified, premium resort portfolio that captures both mass and premium customers. Geographic and product diversification (gaming, rooms, retail, events) stabilizes revenue sources over cycles and supports structural demand.

bull.t: Strategic growth pipeline with regulatory backing
bull.b: Approved land concession and underway Al Marjan work show tangible, long-term capacity expansion. Regulatory authorization for Macau growth and committed UAE development create multi-year revenue drivers and enhance destination competitiveness when projects come online.

bear.b: A heavily debt‑supported capital structure and persistent negative equity restrict financial flexibility, increase refinancing and interest-rate vulnerability, and elevate solvency risk in economic stress, limiting ability to absorb shocks or opportunistically fund growth without external capital.

Material incremental equity and CapEx commitments for Al Marjan and Macau entertainment projects raise funding demands. Given elevated debt, these sizable outlays could force further leverage, asset sales, or equity issuance, complicating long-term capital allocation and shareholder returns.

bear.t: Earnings volatility from hold and rising OpEx
bear.b: Gaming revenue is inherently volatile due to hold variability, and rising operating costs (wage and service inflation) compress margins. This structural mix of hold-driven swings and OpEx inflation makes earnings less predictable and pressure sustained margin expansion over time.
